paper.title_en: Regularization in Scattering from Dirac Delta Potential with Minimal Length
paper.abstract_en: The scattering of a quantum particle by a two or three-dimensional Dirac delta potential leads to divergent integrals, rendering the cross section ill-defined and requiring an ad hoc regularization scheme. We demonstrate that this problem is naturally resolved by invoking a minimal length scale, as predicted by models of quantum gravity and encoded in a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP). This cutoff regularizes the theory and yields finite s-wave scattering amplitudes and cross sections without the introduction of any external regulator or additional parameters. Moreover, we derive an upper bound on the minimal length based on the resonance energy in proton-proton scattering.
